scenes.heading: Unstructured Data
scenes.narration: Unstructured data has no predefined schema or organized format, which makes up the majority of the data organizations collect.

scenes.heading: What it looks like
bullets: Text documents, emails, and chat logs
No rows, columns, or fixed fields
scenes.narration: Unstructured data includes text like documents and emails that carry meaning in free form. It also includes rich media such as images, audio, and video. None of it fits into neat rows and columns with fixed fields. As a result, it usually needs specialized processing before it can be analyzed.

scenes.heading: Making unstructured data usable
scenes.narration: Unstructured data is first stored as raw files, often in a data lake. Engineers then extract features and attach metadata to describe the content. From there, machine learning and search tools can analyze it, unlocking the value hidden inside.

scenes.heading: Structured vs unstructured
scenes.narration: Structured data is a small but highly organized slice that SQL can query directly. Unstructured data is a far larger share of what organizations hold, but it lacks any schema. Extracting value from it requires machine learning, search, or other specialized techniques.

scenes.text: Unstructured data is the largest and richest data type, but it needs extra processing to unlock its value.
scenes.narration: The main lesson is that unstructured data is abundant and valuable, yet it demands extra processing before it yields insight.
